label: Groupoids of Local Isometries
notes: This final section of Part III, printed pages 584 to 619, repackages local symmetry as a category. Patches of a metric space are objects, isometries between open subsets are arrows, and orbifold and developability questions become statements about that groupoid. Set the agenda: pseudogroup, germ groupoid, etale viewpoint, developability.

label: Pseudogroups of Local Isometries
notes: Start concretely. A pseudogroup collects partial isometries between open subsets of a space, closed under restriction, inverse, composition where defined, and gluing of compatible pieces. Emphasize that elements are only locally defined, so composition is partial. This partiality is exactly what forces us out of groups and into groupoids.

label: From Pseudogroup to Groupoid
notes: Promote the pseudogroup to a groupoid by taking germs. An arrow is a germ of a local isometry at a point, with source and target the underlying points. Composition of germs is now total wherever targets match. Stress the source and target maps; they are the structural skeleton every later definition hangs on.

label: The Germ and Holonomy Groupoid
notes: Two local isometries agreeing near a point share a germ, so germs quotient out irrelevant domain choices. The isotropy group at a point, arrows from that point to itself, is its holonomy. Explain that holonomy measures how the space sees itself locally, the seed of orbifold singular points and of nontrivial local symmetry.

label: The Etale Viewpoint
notes: Give the topology. Germs carry a sheaf-like topology making source and target local homeomorphisms; such a groupoid is etale. Walk through why this is the right setting: the arrow space is locally modelled on the object space, so the groupoid is genuinely low dimensional and behaves like a space with extra symmetry arrows.

label: Orbifolds as Groupoids
notes: Connect to orbifolds. A proper, properly discontinuous action of a group by isometries yields a quotient whose local structure is recorded by the action groupoid. Charts model neighbourhoods as quotients of balls by finite isotropy. The orbifold is not just the quotient space but the quotient together with this groupoid of local symmetries.

label: Complexes of Groups
notes: Tie to Part III machinery. A complex of groups over a scwol assigns groups to cells and injections to faces, the combinatorial shadow of an orbifold's local groups. The associated groupoid assembles these local groups and gluing maps. Developable complexes of groups are exactly those arising from an actual group action on a simply connected complex.

label: Equivalence of Groupoids
notes: Insist the groupoid, not its object space, is the real invariant. Two groupoids are equivalent when an essential, fully faithful functor relates them, so refining a cover or changing charts gives an equivalent groupoid. Morita equivalence is the precise notion. Geometric quantities we care about must be equivalence invariants, like the fundamental group below.

label: The Fundamental Groupoid
notes: Define homotopy for the groupoid. A path alternates short geodesic moves with arrows, and the fundamental group collects such loops up to homotopy. For a developable orbifold this recovers the deck group of the universal cover. Emphasize this is the algebraic gatekeeper: it controls whether local pieces can unfold consistently.

label: Developability
notes: State the main theme. The space is developable when the local charts assemble into a global development, a simply connected space on which the groupoid acts so the original is the quotient. The obstruction is holonomy around loops. Non-positive curvature of the local model is the hypothesis that kills the obstruction and forces developability.

label: The Development via Lifted Geodesics
notes: Make developability constructive. Build the development by lifting geodesics from a basepoint, attaching charts along each lifted path, and identifying overlaps by the recorded germs. Local CAT(0) geometry guarantees lifts are unique and the construction is consistent, so the development is CAT(0) and the orbifold cover exists. This is the notebook's lifted geodesic lab.

label: Synthesis and Takeaways
notes: Close the loop. Pseudogroup gives germs, germs give an etale groupoid, equivalence makes it chart independent, the fundamental groupoid measures holonomy, and non-positive curvature certifies developability into an orbifold cover. Leave the audience with the slogan: a groupoid of local isometries is a space remembering exactly how its patches are symmetric.
